analysis_role: Post-result resolution sensitivity using only already-frozen occurrence assets and the same mutually adjusted BIO15/BIO1 + latitude/longitude Brownian models.

interpretation.bio15: The positive adjusted BIO15 direction survives all six full-topology fits at n>=5 and n>=3, but it becomes much smaller than in the n>=10 panel, fails the all-LOO specificity rule, and adds no held-out BIO15 predictive information beyond BIO1 plus geography. The lack of BIO15 specificity is therefore not explained by n=9 alone.
interpretation.bio1: The negative BIO1 orientation coefficient remains 6/6 and all-LOO directionally stable in both expanded panels after conditioning on BIO15 and geography. This makes BIO1 the more deletion-stable component of the composite present-day climate regime, but its P values remain above conventional thresholds and it is not a demonstrated cause.
interpretation.causal_boundary: Present orientation is associated with a composite climatic/lineage regime rather than a uniquely identified precipitation-seasonality axis. Additional coarse climate-variable fishing is not justified by these results.

claim_ceiling: The n>=10 result remains the primary occurrence-quality analysis; n>=5 and n>=3 are resolution sensitivities.
Direction stability does not establish statistical confirmation, climatic selection, adaptation, plasticity or historical causation.
BIO1 being more deletion-stable than BIO15 does not identify temperature as the causal agent.
Lower occurrence counts increase centroid uncertainty and do not constitute independent replication.
No new occurrence source, taxon alias or environmental predictor was added.
